Activate weft in a project's documents

Source: R/setup.R
use_setup.Rd

Sets up the activation of weft (rule 9.2): the project .Rprofile that calls weft_setup() in every knit, or the same call in each document's front matter, together with the _weft.yml that records the weft version. It says what it will write before it writes anything, and running it again changes nothing. suppressMessages() silences it.

Usage

use_setup(path = ".", route = c("auto", "rprofile", "front-matter"))

Arguments

path

A folder or one document. Default: the current folder.

route

"auto", "rprofile" or "front-matter".

Value

The paths written, relative to the root, invisibly (character() when nothing changed).

Details

path is a folder or one .qmd, .Rmd or .rmd file. A folder in a Quarto project (a _quarto.yml here or above it) is set up at the project root. The route is "rprofile" in a Quarto project and "front-matter" otherwise, unless you choose.

It writes:

  • _weft.yml, when there is none (a comment and weft_version:), or the weft_version: line appended to one that lacks it. An existing line is left as it is.

  • route "rprofile": the .Rprofile at the project root. A new file sources ~/.Rprofile first, because R reads one profile only; an existing file gains a comment and the activation line after its last line (after source("renv/activate.R"), so weft is found in renv's library). A file that already calls weft::weft_setup() is kept.

  • route "front-matter": knitr: opts_knit: weft: !expr weft::weft_setup() in each document's front matter.

  • engine: knitr in each .qmd that has no engine: or jupyter: key and is not another engine's alone (a Python-only page stays Jupyter), except files and folders whose names start with _ or . (includes).

  • for an .Rmd outside a Quarto project, weft-check.lua beside the document (weft's own file: kept when identical, replaced when it differs) and, under each format of output:, pandoc_args: ["--lua-filter", "weft-check.lua"].

Front matter is edited as text and checked by parsing it again. When an edit cannot be made safely (flow-style knitr: or pandoc_args, a YAML anchor, another weft: value under opts_knit), or a file's place holds a folder or a symbolic link, nothing is written, and the error prints the lines to add by hand.
